course_description:
This course focuses on dogs, cats and exotic animal species, the human-animal bond, and the role of pets in society. Students learn about the biology, behaviour and management of cattle, dogs, cats, companion birds, rodent pets, reptiles, and other exotic species. The course also explores topical issues about these species. Students will gain the required skills to enable them to competently handle and restrain common domestic and exotic animal species in this course. After completing this course, students will have the essential knowledge, understanding and skills required for them to successfully complete their Animal Husbandry Pre-clinical Work Integrated Learning (AH/PC WIL) placements.

ANIM1120 is a foundational lecture and practical based course which provides knowledge and understanding of the principles behind the behaviour, husbandry and management of common domestic animals - cattle, dogs and cats in addition to various rodent, reptile and exotic animal species. This course covers the role of pets in society and includes lectures on dogs, cats, birds (including backyard poultry), fish, reptiles and other exotic pet species. Practical activity on comparative anatomy where students will dissect a variety of specimens is included in this course. Activity based practicals involve group teaching which will involve hands-on interaction including handling, restraint. This practical component of the course will focus on preparing students to enable them to competently and safely complete their Animal Husbandry Pre-clinical Work Integrated Learning (AH/PC WIL) placements and be able to progress to training in the clinical examination ofﾠanimals. ﾠﾠ

course_aims:
This course provides students with a sound understanding of anatomy and physiology of common domestic and exotic animal species, including cattle, dogs, cats, birds (including backyard poultry), fish and other exotic species. Students will gain specific knowledge on the principles behind the behaviour, husbandry and management of domestic animal species and common exotic species.

Students will develop practical handling skills and understanding of professional responsibilities. This course provides students with the foundational knowledge and understanding required to complete the pre-clinical placements (Extra-Mural Studies [EMS]) required of the BVetTech program.

learning_outcomes.description: Explain the fundamental anatomy and physiology of various domestic and exotic animal species.

Describe the role of pets in society and be able to identify the common breeds of domestic and exotic animal species, and recognise the major topical issues around pet ownership, including preventative health programs, animal behaviour and husbandry, and practical competencies from a safety perspective relevant to industry engagement.
Describe wildlife management practices and develop an understanding of wildlife professional responsibilities and ethical considerations
Review and critically appraise peer-reviewed veterinary literature.

learning_activities.topic: Comparative anatomy practicals and Animal behaviour, handling and restraint practicals involving cattle, dogs, cats, avian and exotics Five scheduled practical classes will be conducted in groups throughout the semester. During the first practical (Weeks 1–4), students will develop their understanding of comparative anatomy through hands-on study of a range of animal species, including ruminants, dogs, cats, birds, reptiles, and other small mammals. From Weeks 5–13, four species-specific handling and restraint practicals will be conducted in parallel. Students will rotate through practical sessions involving cattle, dogs, cats, avian and exotics, gaining experience in safe and appropriate handling and restraint techniques. Each student will be scheduled to attend each practical session once during the semester, ensuring exposure to all species groups. Sub-activity: Group wise - Comparative anatomy of dogs, cats and avian and exotic animal species - Week 1 - 4 Group wise - Animal handling - Week 5 -13

Lectures Lecture series on companion animal and exotic pet behavior, handling and management Sub-activity: Comparative anatomy of ruminants, dogs, cats and avian and exotic animal species - Week 1 Companion animal handling & restraint - Week 2 to 3 Avian and exotics animal species and their husbandry - Week 3 to 8 Dog sports & service dogs - Week 9 Companion animal nutrition, husbandry, housing & enrichment - Week 10 to 11 Industry placements lecture - Week 11
Applied animal behaviour assignment and presentation Presentation preparation on a given topic and submission. To be completed in Week 5 to 12
Cat protection society of UK online learning course Self-directed learning module. To be completed in week 8 and 10.
